name: South America: Argentina

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will learn the history, general climate, major wine regions, and grape varieties of Argentina.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will have a deeper knowledge of the winemaking regions of Argentina and factors of its unique terroirs. A Certified Sommelier will be able to recognize iconic producers and be able to recommend and sell food pairings with wines from Argentina to a guest.

rows.intro: Located in South America, east of the Andes Mountain Range and west of the Atlantic Ocean.
Andes Mountains are an average of 900 meters / 3,000 feet above sea level and create a rain shadow.
rows.certified: Salta is 1500-2000 meters / 5,000-6,000 feet in elevation, the highest in Argentina.; Mendoza is 600-1200 meters / 2,000-4,000 feet in elevation.

rows.intro: Irrigation is essential and flood irrigation or modern drip irrigation is used. Melted snow from the Andes provides a water source. Major diurnal shifts.
rows.certified: Malbec can have an electric purple color due to increased sun exposure at higher elevations causing intense pigmentation.

rows.intro: Torrontés commonly has no oak influence.; New or used, French or American oak are all common for Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon.
85% min to list the grape variety on a label.

Salta:; Subregion: Cafayate known for Torrontés.; Mendoza:; Subregions: Luján de Cuyo and Uco Valley known for Malbec.; Patagonia: Cool due to southern latitude.; Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir
Torrontés is a highly aromatic grape with soapy, floral, and fruity flavors. It has medium-plus to high acidity making it unique amongst other varieties.

rows.certified: IG: Indicación Geográficas, GIs in English; DOC: Denominación de Origen Controlada system
Know a couple of producers for service exam recommendations.

rows.intro: Vineyards were revitalized by Italian and Spanish immigrants.

rows.certified: Some high-end Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon can benefit from decanting.
Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon pair well with steak and chimichurri.
